steps: Cut a few slits in the brinjal, push a clove of garlic into them and rub it with a little oil.
Roast it straight over a gas flame, turning often, until the skin is black and the inside is soft.
Let it cool a little, peel off the skin and mash the flesh with the roasted garlic.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the cumin, then the chopped ginger, garlic and green chilli.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the chilli powder and coriander powder.
Add the tomato and cook until it turns mushy.
Mix in the mashed brinjal and salt and cook on low for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring often.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves and serve with roti.
note: The sources disagree a lot on eggplant: one uses 100 g a person, the other about 275 g. 200 g of raw eggplant was kept as a fair middle, since it shrinks a lot once roasted and peeled; garlic comes down from 8.5 g to 5 g.
